A transformer decoder generates text autoregressively: it produces one token at a time, feeds that token back as input, and repeats. The raw tokens are first mapped to dense vectors via an embedding matrix. Each token's row in this matrix is looked up, producing a vector of dimension *d_model*. Because the architecture has no inherent sense of order, a positional encoding (in modern LLMs, typically a learned absolute or relative position embedding, or RoPE rotations) is added to each token vector. The result is a sequence of vectors, one per previous token, that the rest of the network will process.
